review: This is the most rigged video game of all time. The level of greed from EA. The lack of respect for the community. The lack of respect for the game of football. And the absence of integrity, it is all very lame and absurd. A video game, especially one where the grind means everything, should reward you with generous loot overtime: the more time you spend in the game, the more loot you get. Instead, all you get is a big finger in the face. Money, money and money. Packs, packs, packs. Why do I play this game, and as much as I do? Because I am a degenerate player. You, my good friend, if you are new and is thinking of giving this game a try, please, no, stay the F...# away from this garbo game. The stench is horrible. The greed is massive. A video game developed to play with your psyche and just trigger dopamine so you will open your wallet. NO! DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME. READ ME! DO... NOT... PLAY... THIS... GAME.

TL:DR - This game is a psychologically manipulative Skinner box. It is designed to be addictive, and to get as much money out of you as possible. Scripting, implemented to encourage FUT players to spend more money, is in every mode and makes every game an unsatisfying and empty experience. Considering a core demographic for this game is children, the income-focused manipulation displayed here is repugnant. 

DDA (dynamic difficulty adjustment) or scipting is just ridiculous now. In games against EA's garbage AI, if the game wants your opponent to score, they'll respond to your controller inputs instantly, not the actions of the player you're controlling (input reading). Easy tackles with world class defenders will either miss, bounce the ball to another opponent, just outright phase through the ball or even the damn player! Your keeper will do a Matrix-esque dodge of a shot coming directly at them or will spill an easy catch directly into their striker. The most outrageous though, is player switching on loose balls and when contesting headers. The game will sometimes prevent you from switching to a player (even manually with the right stick) if they're close enough to win a loose ball or are in the best position to win a header. They will instead just stand there, staring blankly into the distance, until the opponent wins back possession. It's the most obvious example of the game cheating to achieve the outcome it wants. This stuff is so obvious that I've been able to predict when a goal is coming, just by how many advantages the AI gets. 

Other examples:
- 30 year old fullback with 60 pace will gain an otherworldly burst of speed to get ahead of my winger with 90 pace
- Players will frequently and deliberately place themselves in a position to lose headers, even if you're instructing them to do the opposite
- Opposition defenders will basically teleport to tackle you the second you press shoot in the box
- Your passes will frequently go to a player in the complete opposite direction to the one you've commanded
- Uncontrolled defenders will randomly clatter someone in the box, giving away a penalty
- Some of the AI's most outrageous Sunday league fouls just won't be given 
- If the game doesn't want you to score anymore (or has the scoreline it wants to achieve), the opposition will just pass the ball around the back or run all the way back to the keeper upon any pressure. This would be fine if they weren't 2-1 down at 70', where any team would be pushing hard for an equaliser. 
- If the game wants you to score, all of these advantages are removed and opposing players lose 50 IQ points. It's ridiculously transparent. 

These problems extend to all other game modes, especially Ultimate Team. 

At the end of the day, all this does is damage the experience. Wins don't feel earned, since it's obvious that the game is allowing you to win. When you lose it's often because of the above advantages, not from been legitimately outplayed. For a game that aims to recreate football, it fails spectacularly in presenting the core part of that experience; the in-match gameplay. Neglecting this, by adding a scripting or variable difficulty system to psychologically manipulate FUT players to spend more money, not only irrevocably destroys the experience in all modes, but is also outrageously anti-consumer. I knew on reputation that EA Sports games were microtransaction ridden hellholes but this is predatory to a degree I've never seen before. Considering a core demographic for this game is children, manipulation like this is repugnant. Honestly, I feel dirty having spent money on this. 

Do not buy this or any other EA Sports Skinner box, it's a prime example of everything wrong with this heinous company.

I don’t usually write reviews, but FC 25 has pushed me to my absolute limit. What was once a franchise with potential has now devolved into a shameless cash-grab, riddled with bugs, glitches, and the kind of technical incompetence that would be laughable—if it weren’t so infuriating.

From the moment I launched the game, it became painfully obvious that quality control was not part of the development process. Menus freeze. Players T-pose mid-match. The ball teleports. Animations glitch out. The Career Mode crashes randomly, and online play is a chaotic mess of lag, disconnections, and exploits that have existed since FC 24—some even earlier.

And let’s talk about gameplay. If it even deserves to be called that. The AI is either brain-dead or omniscient, with no in-between. Referees make decisions that defy all logic. Player movements feel like controlling a sack of bricks, and don’t get me started on the goalkeepers—they either let everything in or suddenly turn into prime Neuer for no apparent reason.

But perhaps the most insulting part of all this is EA’s ongoing obsession with monetization over quality. Ultimate Team is still the primary focus, of course—stuffed with microtransactions and pay-to-win nonsense, while actual game stability and realism are treated like afterthoughts.

This game isn’t a step forward. It’s a slap in the face to anyone who expected progress or even basic functionality. It's not just disappointing—it's broken, lazy, and borderline unplayable. I paid full price for what amounts to an early-access beta at best.

To the developers: fix your game. To EA: stop insulting your player base. And to prospective buyers: don’t waste your money or your time. FC 25 is an embarrassment.

EA Sports FC 25 – A Disgrace to Football Gaming

EA Sports FC 25 is, without a doubt, one of the most disappointing and infuriating football games ever released. It’s an absolute embarrassment to the franchise, plagued with lazy design, horrendous gameplay mechanics, and an overbearing focus on microtransactions.

Gameplay – A Broken Mess

Playing EA FC 25 feels like wrestling with a game engine that actively works against you. Passing is completely unreliable, with simple five-yard passes veering off target like a Sunday League disasterclass. The attacking AI is beyond incompetent—your forwards stand still like mannequins while defenders teleport to intercept through balls with unnatural precision.

Defending? Forget about it. Manual defending is utterly useless because the game rewards reckless AI-assisted jockeying instead of actual skill. Tackling rarely works, and even when you win the ball, your player fumbles it back to the opponent like a scripted comedy sketch.

Graphics & Presentation – Stale and Lifeless

For a game that prides itself on realism, FC 25 looks shockingly outdated. Player models remain stiff and lifeless, stadiums lack any atmosphere, and animations are still riddled with awkward, robotic movements. EA has barely touched the Career Mode experience, leaving it feeling like an afterthought—stale, neglected, and unplayable.

Technical Disaster – Glitches and Lag

Navigating the menus feels like playing a game from the early 2000s. Lag, freezes, and unresponsive controls make basic tasks a nightmare. Matches are filled with bizarre glitches, from invisible players to goalkeepers diving the wrong way. Worse, crashes are so common that you’d think the game was still in beta.

Ultimate Scam Mode (Ultimate Team)

Ultimate Team has become nothing more than a cash grab. Pack odds are horrendous, rewards are minimal, and the entire mode is designed to frustrate players into spending real money. The new “Evolutions” feature is a blatant attempt to extract more money while adding absolutely no real depth to the game.

Final Verdict – An Unforgivable Failure

FC 25 is yet another disappointing entry in a series that seems to get worse each year. EA promised improvements — what we got is a barely functional, bug-filled mess that heavily favors those who spend the most money, not those who actually play well.

Let’s start with the bugs: broken animations, players sliding across the pitch, menus freezing, constant stuttering, and random crashes. It honestly feels like an early beta rather than a full-priced release in 2025.

But it gets worse — the online gameplay is infested with cheaters. Speed hacks, superhuman AI, rigged ball physics — and the worst part? There’s no way to report them in-game. No report button. No fair anti-cheat system. And if you try to go through EA’s support? Good luck getting anything other than a generic, automated response that leads nowhere.

Even if you avoid the cheaters, you're still up against FC 25’s blatantly pay-to-win mechanics. Players who drop hundreds (or thousands) on packs are gifted overpowered squads, unreal pace, and unfair boosts. You can grind all you want, but if you don’t pay, you’re always a step behind. Skill takes a backseat to how deep your wallet is.

This isn’t a football game — it’s a slot machine in disguise. A broken, exploit-ridden, unbalanced experience that rewards spending, not talent.

In short: FC 25 is frustrating, unfair, and simply not worth your time or money. Unless you enjoy being punished for playing fair, stay away.
